subjectLine: Apache mod_http2 RCE Under Active Attack, OpenSSH 'sshole' Exploited, and Microsoft's Record Patch Tuesday
weekIntro: This week presents an aggressive barrage of infrastructure threats led by active in-the-wild exploitation of Apache's HTTP/2 engine and OpenSSH authentication on musl-based distributions. Simultaneously, Microsoft released a massive Patch Tuesday addressing actively targeted zero-days, while high-impact supply-chain attacks struck Red Hat Quay and thousands of GitHub CI/CD workflows. Security teams should immediately triage internet-facing endpoints, rotate exposed automation tokens, and apply pending hypervisor and runtime fixes.

articles.title: Critical Remote Code Execution Flaw in Apache HTTP Server’s HTTP/2 Module Patched
articles.summary: Apache HTTP Server 2.4.55‑2.4.70 with mod_http2 enabled contains a critical unauthenticated RCE vulnerability (CVE‑2026‑119618) that is actively exploited; the issue is fixed in Apache 2.4.71 and corresponding distro packages.
articles.impact: Unauthenticated attackers can execute arbitrary code on vulnerable web servers, potentially taking full control of the server process. Exploits work against default configurations with HTTP/2 enabled, posing immediate risk to internet‑facing services.
articles.action: Upgrade to Apache HTTP Server 2.4.71 or apply the vendor‑specific patches (e.g., mod_http2‑2.0.26‑7.el9_9.1 for RHEL) and disable HTTP/2 if you cannot patch immediately.

articles.title: Microsoft November 2026 Patch Tuesday Fixes Over 1,250 Flaws, Including Actively Exploited Outlook Zero‑Day
articles.summary: Microsoft released November Patch Tuesday addressing 1,259‑1,260 CVEs across Windows, Office, Edge, Exchange, SharePoint, LDAP, AD DS, Hyper‑V and .NET, with 68 critical bugs. A spoofing zero‑day in Outlook (CVE‑2026‑124194) is already being exploited to steal NTLMv2 hashes, and multiple remote‑code‑execution flaws affect LDAP, AD DS and Hyper‑V.
articles.impact: Security teams face immediate risk of credential theft and domain‑wide compromise if the Outlook zero‑day or the LDAP/AD DS RCE bugs are not patched, while unpatched privilege‑escalation flaws in Hyper‑V and Edge could enable attacker persistence and lateral movement.
articles.action: Deploy the November updates across all Windows, Office, Edge, Exchange, SharePoint, LDAP, AD DS and Hyper‑V endpoints without delay.

articles.title: Active Exploitation of OpenSSH “sshole” Flaw Grants Unauthenticated Remote Access
articles.summary: The newly disclosed sshole vulnerability in OpenSSH, triggered by a musl library interaction, is being actively exploited to bypass authentication and obtain privileged SSH access on vulnerable Linux devices, with attacks observed in Southeast Asian honeypots.
articles.impact: Security teams must assume that any Linux host running OpenSSH with musl is at immediate risk of remote compromise and that attackers are already deploying a backdoor called TAC Agent for persistence.
articles.action: Deploy the OpenSSH patch released today and verify that musl‑linked binaries are updated or replaced on all affected systems.

articles.title: Critical Red Hat Quay Flaws Allow Unauthenticated Reading and Overwriting of Private Container Images
articles.summary: Two critical vulnerabilities in Red Hat Quay (CVE‑2026‑123710 CVSS 9.8 and CVE‑2026‑110697 CVSS 9.9) let any attacker with registry access read, delete, or overwrite private images and steal robot‑account tokens.
articles.impact: Security teams risk credential leakage, supply‑chain compromise, and service disruption across every environment pulling from compromised registries.
articles.action: Update all Quay instances to the fixed builds released by Red Hat immediately and rotate all image signing keys and robot‑account tokens.

articles.title: Hijacked GitHub Accounts Deploy CI Secret Stealer Across 1,800+ Repositories
articles.summary: A threat group dubbed wfx-loot compromised 4,837 GitHub accounts and injected a secret‑stealing script into at least 1,806 repositories, harvesting CI pipeline secrets and cloud credentials.
articles.impact: All CI/CD secrets and cloud roles accessible to the affected workflows should be considered compromised, exposing downstream services and infrastructure to credential abuse.
articles.action: Audit all recent GitHub account activity, enforce MFA, rotate CI secrets, and scan repositories for unauthorized workflow or npm hook modifications.

articles.title: Check Point Gateways Compromised via PHP2Shell Exploits and Gaia OS Privilege Escalation
articles.summary: Unpatched Check Point Security Gateways were breached using PHP2Shell flaws, followed by a local privilege escalation (CVE-2026-123039) in Gaia OS that granted root access and allowed deployment of the persistent TSGA backdoor.
articles.impact: Security teams must assume that any affected Check Point appliance could be fully compromised, with attackers able to install web shells, backdoors, and destructive wiper malware across the network.
articles.action: Apply the latest patches for the PHP2Shell and CVE-2026-123039 vulnerabilities immediately and audit all Check Point gateways for unauthorized shells and the TSGA backdoor.

articles.title: Git Fixes Critical Integer Truncation Vulnerability (CVE‑2026‑111760) in 2.56.1 and Back‑ported Releases
articles.summary: Git’s integer truncation flaw (CVE‑2026‑111760) allowed malicious repositories to execute attacker‑controlled code during recursive clones and submodule fetches. The vulnerability is patched in Git 2.56.1 and back‑ported to 2.50.2, 2.51.3, 2.52.1, 2.53.1, 2.54.1, and 2.55.1. Immediate upgrade is required.
articles.impact: Security teams must treat any Git clone operation as potentially hostile, especially when pulling untrusted repositories or using recursive submodule fetches, because the flaw could inject malicious hooks via crafted path names.
articles.action: Upgrade all Git installations to 2.56.1 or the appropriate back‑ported version and enforce trusted‑source cloning policies.

articles.title: SignDrop Windows Zero‑Day Grants Full SYSTEM Privileges via Windows Defender Abuse
articles.summary: The SignDrop kernel vulnerability lets any local user elevate to full SYSTEM rights on Windows 10, 11, and Server 2022 by coercing Windows Defender to create a privileged CLFS log...
articles.impact: Security teams face immediate risk of full system compromise on affected Windows installations, with attackers able to bypass existing defenses and execute arbitrary code as SYSTEM.
articles.action: Deploy Microsoft’s out‑of‑band patch immediately and block untrusted CLFS container creation by Windows Defender until remediation is applied.

articles.title: Critical Pre‑Auth Use‑After‑Free in MongoDB Can Crash Replica Set Members on Failover (CVE‑2026‑118383)
articles.summary: MongoDB Server contains a pre‑authentication use‑after‑free flaw (CVE‑2026‑118383) that lets an unauthenticated attacker trigger a crash during replica set failover, causing denial‑of‑service. The vulnerability scores 9.5/10 CVSS 4.
articles.impact: Any MongoDB deployment using replica sets, sharded clusters, or config servers is vulnerable to unexpected crashes when a compromised node is elected primary, potentially disrupting applications and data availability.
articles.action: Upgrade every member of each replica set to the fixed MongoDB release immediately and verify version consistency across all nodes, including containers and offline instances.

articles.title: Mior and Skyfall Attacks Break AMD SEV‑SNP Confidential Computing
articles.summary: Researchers demonstrated two attacks, Mior and Skyfall, that let a rogue hypervisor read and modify memory inside AMD SEV‑SNP‑protected VMs.
articles.impact: These exploits defeat AMD’s hardware‑enforced isolation, exposing secrets and allowing undetectable VM manipulation, forcing administrators to treat SEV‑SNP as compromised until patches are applied.
articles.action: Apply the BIOS and firmware updates released by AMD and your server vendor immediately and verify the integrity of SEV‑SNP configurations.
